catalog_quote: [Corston-Oliver 2002 §1.3] Stress is not contrastive. Stress is assigned independently to roots and to material which precedes the root (i.e. prefixes and reduplicated material) as follows: (i) Roots of one syllable, with the exception of prepositions and articles, take stress ... (ii) Roots of two syllables are stressed on the initial syllable: /'zama/ 'talk' /'talo/ 'taro' ... (iii) Roots of more than two syllables are stressed on the first and second syllables: /'e'hara/ 'blood' /'zi'para/ 'red' /'ga'loto/ 'struggle' /'si'gareti/ 'cigarette' /'ba'sioto/ 'crocodile' ... All material which precedes the root (prefixes and reduplicated material) is assigned stress as if it were a single root. ... The transitive suffix /-i/ takes stress ... Other suffixes, however, do not take stress, and are ignored in determining the placement of stress. ... Finally, stress is assigned independently to …

audit.recode_to: Resolve 'descriptions disagree' in favour of Corston-Oliver 2002 (the record's own stated fallback: MORPHOLOGICAL / left-edge root-initial, non-contrastive), keeping Schuelke 2020's penult note as a flagged provisional dissent; add Waterhouse 1928 p. ix as third primary.
audit.reasoning: (1) Both deciding quotations are verbatim in held files at the stated locators; the 2002 passage was additionally checked against a clean page image (print p. 469), which also shows that Corston-Oliver marks syllables 1 and 2 of long roots with identical primary marks, so no ranking can be read into it. (2) The coding rests on the best descriptions that exist: a 2002 handbook sketch with a real stress section and a 2020 syntax dissertation with a self-declared provisional stress paragraph; Glottolog has no grammar/phonology above sketch level and Crossref shows no phonology or instrumental study. (3) Opening the remaining Glottolog items: Corston 1996, Ray 1926 and Todd 2000 are silent; Waterhouse 1928 (PARADISEC images, fetched sources) states 'the accent in the great majority of cases falls on the first syllable', an independent third primary that agrees with Corston-Oliver's left-edge account
audit.second_reader_evidence: QUOTES (re-opened, all verbatim): (1) Corston-Oliver 2002 sec. 1.3: held scanned lines 42320-42410 carries every sentence of the catalog quote, header 'ROVIANA 469' falls after the first two sentences so pp. 468-469 is right; the fetched sources clean page render (printed p. 469) shows /'e'hara/, /'zi'ŋara/ (scanned 'zi'para'), /'ga'loto/, /'si'gareti/, /'ba'sioto/ with two identical raised primary marks, so the other first reader is right that no primary/secondary ranking is recoverable from print. (2) Schuelke 2020: held schuelke2020_
